results.reply: parse_port strips surrounding whitespace, treats None or an empty/whitespace-only value as the 3000 default, accepts only ASCII digits 0-9 (str.isdigit alone is rejected because it also accepts Unicode digits), converts to int, and requires 1 through 65535. Anything else raises ValueError with the offending text. Validation plan, not yet executed: (1) None, "", "   ", "\t\n" -> 3000; (2) "80", " 8080 ", "1", "65535", "0080" -> 80, 8080, 1, 65535, 80; (3) "0", "65536", "99999" -> ValueError; (4) "-1", "+80", "80a", "8 0", "3000.0", "abc", "0x1F" -> ValueError; (5) Unicode digits such as Arabic-Indic "٨٠" or superscript "²" -> ValueError; (6) confirm the existing config helper's call sites pass either None or str and that the raised exception surfaces the raw value in its message.

The bug: the dict comprehension keeps the LAST record for each id, because later entries overwrite the value while the key keeps its first position. So order looked right but the wrong object was returned. The fix tracks seen ids in a set and appends only the first occurrence, preserving input order, returning the original objects untouched, and never mutating the input. Regression cases to add (not yet run): (1) duplicates with differing payloads, e.g. [{id:'a',v:1},{id:'b',v:2},{id:'a',v:3}] returns the v:1 and v:2 objects in that order, and the returned 'a' is the identical object (assert `is`); (2) empty list returns []; (3) no duplicates returns an equal-length list in the same order; (4) input list and its records are unchanged after the call (compare a deep copy taken beforehand); (5) any iterable input such as a generator or tuple works; (6) ids that differ only by case or whitespace are treated as distinct; (7) all records sharing one id returns exactly the first.
